The list of PTE accepted universities in Canada is long, but “accepted” rarely means one fixed score. Each institution and each programme sets its own overall and component bar, and a few faculties do not take PTE at all.

PTE Academic has become a common alternative to IELTS and TOEFL for international students, and Canadian admissions offices treat it as a valid measure of English. This guide gives you the list, the score ranges to plan around, and where the test fits alongside your study permit for the 2027 cycle.

Quick Answer: Is PTE Accepted in Canada?

The short answer is yes. PTE Academic works at a wide range of Canadian institutions and colleges as proof of English for admission. Most ask for an overall score, and many also set a minimum in each of the four skills: reading, writing, listening and speaking.

A single number rarely tells the whole story. You can meet the overall bar and still fall short if one component sits below the required minimum. The list of PTE accepted universities in Canada keeps growing, but the requirement varies case by case, so confirm it on the official page before you apply.

PTE Academic vs PTE Core

If your goal is a degree, book PTE Academic. Booking the wrong test means paying twice.

A quick read of that table: 65 overall with 60 in each skill is the most common benchmark at the top-ranked schools, while several institutions sit lower for general entry. That small detail about component minimums matters, so the next section explains overall versus skill scores in plain terms.

Typical PTE Score Requirement in Canada

There is no single pass mark. Planning ranges still help you judge where you stand before you sit the test. The table below groups typical expectations by study level across Canadian universities that accept PTE.

Study level

Typical PTE Academic planning range

Diploma/college

50–60

Undergraduate

58–65

Master’s / postgraduate

60–70

Competitive programmes

65–75+

Read these as planning ranges, not admission rules. Health, nursing, law, business, education and competitive STEM programmes often sit at the top of each band or above it. The overall score is only half the picture. You can score 65 overall and still be refused if the programme wants 60 in every skill and one component comes in at 58. Check both numbers, every time.

Timing works in your favour with this test. Results usually arrive within 48 hours of the sitting, and you send them to institutions electronically through your Pearson account, typically at no extra cost per recipient.

Scores stay valid for two years, and if a component falls short, you can usually rebook as soon as the result lands. That quick loop makes PTE a practical choice when a deadline is close, provided a test-centre slot is available near you.

How to Choose a Canadian University with PTE

The test score should not lead your search. The programme decides everything downstream: the academic prerequisites, the intake months, and the exact English bar you have to clear, so settle the programme first.

From your shortlist, work through five checks. Confirm the programme takes PTE Academic, not only IELTS; if it does not, TOEFL and Duolingo are the usual fallbacks, so keep other English test options in view. Read the overall score and the component minimum, since the second one catches people out.

Look at the intake and its deadline, because January, May and September intakes vary by school. Confirm whether scores must be sent directly from Pearson. Then weigh tuition and permit costs together, because the cheapest tuition is not always the cheapest year, as a look at the more affordable universities in Canada quickly shows.

If two options fit, let the component minimum and the intake timing break the tie.

Undergraduate Students: What to Check

Undergraduate admission rests on two pillars: your academic record and your English. For the academic side, you generally need Grade 12 or an equivalent qualification that meets the programme’s prerequisites.

On English, most Canadian schools that take PTE publish an overall score and a per-skill minimum for first-year entry. Confirm both, then check whether your programme adds subject prerequisites on top. Deadlines matter as much as scores here, since popular programmes fill early and some close well before the intake month.

A test waiver exists at a few schools if you studied in English, much as some Canada options without IELTS work, but only where the institution allows it. Do not assume a waiver applies to you until the admissions page says so.

Master’s Students: What to Check

Graduate admission runs through two gates: the university’s minimum and the department’s own bar. The department bar is usually higher, and it is the one that decides your file.

Watch three things in particular. Some schools do not take PTE for graduate entry at all, McGill among them for most graduate programmes, so verify this before you book the test.

Is PTE Accepted for Canada Study Permit?

To apply for a study permit you need a Letter of Acceptance from a Designated Learning Institution, or DLI. Most college and undergraduate applicants also need a Provincial or Territorial Attestation Letter, the PAL or TAL. As of January 2026, master’s and doctoral students at public DLIs are exempt from that step. You must also show proof of funds: for applicants outside Quebec the living-cost figure is CAD 22,895 for a single student, on top of first-year tuition and travel.

That amount is set for the 2026 cycle, so check the current figure before you apply. Meeting the English requirement does not guarantee a permit.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

A few common errors can delay an application, add cost, or affect an offer. Watch for these.

  • Assuming one score works everywhere, when each programme sets its own.
  • Reading only the overall score and ignoring the component minimums.
  • Trusting outdated score lists on blogs instead of the official page.
  • Skipping faculty-level rules that sit above the stated minimum.
  • Believing a good result guarantees a study permit. It does not.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is PTE accepted in Canada universities?

Yes. PTE Academic works at many Canadian institutions and colleges as proof of English. The rules and the required score are set case by case, so confirm the figure on the official page.

What PTE score is required for Canada?

There is no single number. Diplomas often sit near 50 to 60, undergraduate entry near 58 to 65, and master’s programmes near 60 to 70. Competitive courses ask for more, so plan for the higher end.

Which Canadian universities accept PTE Academic?

Toronto, UBC, McGill, Alberta, Waterloo, Queen’s, Calgary, Ottawa and York all take PTE Academic for at least some programmes, alongside many others. Always check the specific programme page before you apply.

Is PTE Core accepted for university admission in Canada?

Can I study in Canada without IELTS if I have PTE?

Often, yes. Where a school takes PTE, it usually replaces IELTS for the English requirement. A few programmes still prefer IELTS or accept Duolingo, so confirm your programme takes PTE first.

Is PTE accepted for Canada study permit?

PTE supports admission, not the permit directly. The study permit depends on your Letter of Acceptance, proof of funds and other documents. A strong score does not by itself secure a permit.

How long is a PTE score valid?

A PTE score is valid for two years from the test date. Most Canadian institutions accept a result only within that two-year window, so time your test to your application.

Final Verdict

For most international students, the list of PTE accepted universities in Canada is long enough that PTE Academic is a safe, well-recognised choice. Verify two numbers for every programme: the overall score and the component minimum.

Remember that admission and the study permit are separate hurdles, and the test clears only the first. Confirm each requirement on the official page, and speak with an adviser before applying if the rules are unclear for your case.
